- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward correction — allow slight lagged rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), model often overestimates mean; apply mean reversion bias toward recent 7-day average.  
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates peak prices; cap forecast at 1.2x recent 14-day high if sentiment is bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows rapid reversal (e.g., 0.9 → 0.1 → 0.8), model should adjust forecast mid-horizon to reflect sentiment shift.  
- Avoid forecasting beyond 20% above recent 30-day high unless sentiment is >0.8 and sustained.  
- If true outcome deviates >15% from forecast in first 5 days, adjust remaining forecast by -10% to -20% for remaining days.
